newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares tumble amid Brazil worries.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares tumble amid Brazil worries.

text.p: Chilean blue chips withered on Tuesday amid fears of a currency devaluation in Brazil, ending nearly two percent lower, brokers said.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares followed other regional indices down, closing 1.92 percent off at 131.25 points. The all-share IGPA index ended 1.4 percent down to 5717.51 points.
After steady gains during the past few weeks, the bourse was ripe for a reversal, but concerns about Brazil made it steeper than it might otherwise have been, brokers said.
"The news from Brazil made people nervous but to some extent it really only accentuated a natural correction in prices," one broker said.

Brazilian officials denied they were planning a devaluation or any changes to the existing foreign currency regime, despite fears that foreign exchange woes affecting some Asian economies would spread to Brazil.

The IPSA's decline, on paltry volume of 9.7 billion pesos, came despite comments by Central Bank President Carlos Massad that fresh data would show May year-over-year economic growth of five percent and continued low inflation.

Shares in the big-volume electrical sector were especially hard hit. Chilgener SA slipped 2.14 percent to 160 pesos, Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA (Endesa) fell 1.16 percent to 307 pesos, and Colbun SA slipped 1.03 percent to 48 pesos.
